issues.problem: The new assertion 'pass-at-version registry stays out of the checkout' checks that ${REPO_ROOT}/.e2e-matrix-pass-at-version.tsv does not exist, not that this test did not create or change it. The old version of this very test wrote that file into every contributor's checkout (it is git-ignored, /.e2e-*), and operators' matrix runs write it there by design (docs/testing/ENTERPRISE-E2E-HOST-CERTIFICATION-METHODOLOGY.md:514). So the test now fails on every such checkout, including the main checkout /home/user/silver-bullet (the file is present there, dated Oct 17), where the orchestrator will run the merged suite: 'make check' goes red with a message that does not say what to do. A false positive is a bug (FIX-BRIEF).
issues.evidence: ls -la /home/user/silver-bullet/.e2e-matrix-pass-at-version.tsv -> present (642 bytes, Oct 17); its rows are row 22 then row 21 written one second apart, three times, exactly what the old test's two dry runs record. In a git-archive copy of 647e27b (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H3b-probe/copy): printf '4\t0.52.0@abc\t/x/ledger.md\t...' > .e2e-matrix-pass-at-version.tsv; bash tests/run-all-tests.sh tests/scripts/test-enterprise-e2e-matrix-internal-gates.sh -> 'FAIL: pass-at-version registry stays out of the checkout', TOTAL 4 passed, 1 failed. Without the pre-existing file: 5/0.
issues.suggested_fix: Record the file's state before the runs and compare after (e.g. before="$(cksum < "$REG" 2>/dev/null || echo absent)" ... assert_eq "registry in the checkout unchanged" "$before" "$(cksum < "$REG" 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"), and additionally assert the row landed in "$FIXTURE/.e2e-matrix-pass-at-version.tsv" if the dry run records one. Keep the inverse check: removing the override from core.sh must still fail the test on a clean checkout.

issues.problem: The venv wrapper embeds the interpreter path unescaped inside a double-quoted /bin/sh string (printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec "%s" "$@"\n'). A venv path containing $, a backtick, " or \ is re-evaluated by sh on every python3 call: $(...) runs, the exec fails with 127, every Python-using test breaks. The symlink it replaced was immune.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H3b-probe/venvq: venv under a directory named 'a$(touch .../PWNED)b'; PATH=<that>/.venv/bin:$PATH bash tests/run-all-tests.sh t/test-q.sh -> wrapper 'exec ".../a$(touch .../PWNED)b/.venv/bin/python3" "$@"', 'exec: .../ab/.venv/bin/python3: not found', exit 127, and PWNED was created.
issues.suggested_fix: Single-quote the path: q=${_entry//\'/\'\\\'\'}; printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec %s "$@"\n' "'$q'" > "$safe_bin/$_name" (or skip the wrapper and fall back to the symlink when the path contains a quote, $, backtick or backslash). Add a case with a space and a $ in the venv path to test-makefile-setup.sh.

issues.problem: R13-03 residual: the check still matches raw text after decoding \u escapes. VS Code parses tasks.json/settings.json as JSONC, so a comment between tokens or the nested settings form evades it.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H3b-probe/wormvar2 (git fixture), bash scripts/check-repo-invariants.sh --root <fixture> --check worm-indicators: reports d/ e/ f/ (unicode escapes) but not a/.vscode/tasks.json '"runOn" /* c */ : "folderOpen"', b/.vscode/tasks.json '"runOn": // c<NL> "folderOpen"', or c/.vscode/settings.json '{"task": {"allowAutomaticTasks": "on"}}'.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip JSONC comments with a string-aware scanner, drop trailing commas, json.loads, walk keys/values (runOptions.runOn == 'folderOpen' at any depth; a 'task.allowAutomaticTasks' key or a 'task' object holding 'allowAutomaticTasks'); flag an unparseable tracked .vscode/*.json or *.code-workspace. Since this repo tracks no .vscode files, flagging any tracked .vscode/tasks.json is an acceptable simpler rule.

issues.problem: hook-references checks only the first script a command names: if a ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} script appears, a bare relative hooks/ or scripts/ path later in the same command is never examined, so the new R9-22 rule can be sidestepped by chaining.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H3b-probe/hookref: hooks.json command 'bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/a.sh" && bash hooks/evil.sh' -> 'PASS hook-references', rc=0.

issues.problem: The ordering checks compare grep line numbers with [[ -lt ]]; an empty result evaluates as 0, so 'prepare mode precedes the tag' passes vacuously if the prepare command disappears from the skill.
issues.evidence: bash -c '[[ "" -lt 5 ]] && echo TRUE' -> TRUE; the test asserts a numeric value only for the validate line.
issues.suggested_fix: assert_match '^[0-9]+$' for prepare, tag, create and publish before comparing.

abuse_analysis.SB_E2E_PASS_AT_VERSION_REGISTRY: Not a new forgery path. The TSV is only a skip cache read by the operator-run scripts/enterprise-e2e/matrix.sh (enterprise_e2e_matrix_should_skip_row_at_version); no hook or release gate reads it (deploy-tier.sh reads ${SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR}/inline-e2e-matrix). Whoever controls the matrix's environment could already set SB_ROOT, SB_E2E_INSTALL_VERSION_KEY or SB_E2E_ROW_PASS_REGISTRY, or write the unguarded, git-ignored default file in the checkout. When the row-pass-registry lib is loaded the JSON registry decides and the TSV is not consulted for skipping. Hook env is not inherited from an agent's Bash call.
